children: Since Tim Cook took over as Apple's CEO in 2011, the iPhone maker's stock has soared more than 2,200%. Annualized, that gives investors a price move of about 23.5% a year, more than twice the annual gain of the Dow industrials and easily more than the S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite.

As Cook prepares to step down from the CEO role tomorrow to make room for incoming chief John Ternus, here's a look at Apple's annualized performance versus tech-stock peers and major indexes, via Dow Jones Market data.
Read more on Cook's legacy here, and dig deeper here on where the tech giant might go next under Ternus.
